source: AAA gasprices.aaa.com national average — $4.29 on Tuesday June 2, 2026 (Day 95), down from the June 1 (Day 94) print of $4.322 and well off the May peak of $4.536 (May 6, via Fox Business) as May's crude collapse (Brent's worst month since 2020) continued feeding through to the pump; mild upward pressure resumed June 3 as Gulf escalation lifted oil back toward $100. Still ~+43% above the $2.99 Feb 28 baseline. Five states (Alaska, Hawaii, Nevada, Oregon, Washington) remain above $5; California is highest near $6.16. The May peak $4.536 stayed below AAA's all-time record of $5.016 (set June 14, 2022). GasBuddy's Patrick De Haan: 'We won't see those [peak] levels until potentially mid-to-late 2027'; pump relief runs 2-3 weeks behind crude. Watson Institute / Costs of War (Brown): Americans have spent ~$401 more per household on gas and diesel since the war began (via CBS). ITEP tracker (May 31): cumulative ~$46.5 billion paid extra to the oil industry since Feb 28; summer-end forecast $825.02/household.
